page.overview:
What is Perenelle Flamel?

Perenelle Flamel (pre-1334–between 1992 and 1996) was a French witch, the wife of famous Philosopher and Alchemist, Nicolas Flamel, who was known for his creation of the Philosopher's Stone. She became known as one of the oldest witches in history through her use of the Elixir of Life, a life extending potion derived from her husband's creation.

Perenelle attended Beauxbatons Academy of Magic in her youth, where she met Nicolas Flamel. They later married, becoming husband and wife. Perenelle and Nicolas drank the Elixir of Life produced by the Philosopher's Stone, the latter's creation, and became functionally immortal until the stone was destroyed centuries later in the late 20th century.

Perenelle and her husband partly funded the construction of the Palace of Beauxbatons and its grounds with alchemist gold. As a result, a fountain named after them stood in the middle of the school park; it was believed to have healing and beautifying properties.

In early 1992, in consultation with Albus Dumbledore, the couple decided to destroy the stone to prevent its use by Lord Voldemort, who had nearly succeeded in stealing it for his own purposes earlier that year. As they were no longer able to produce the Elixir of Life, she and Nicolas passed away after their supply ran out.
